title: Stewardship
definition: Stewardship is the faithful management of everything God entrusts to a believer for His glory and the good of others.
summary: Stewardship is the faithful management of everything God entrusts to a believer for His glory and the good of others.
christFocus: Jesus is Lord over all of life, and He teaches His servants to use what they have received faithfully until He returns.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Stewardship begins with the truth that everything belongs to God. Time, money, abilities, influence, suffering, opportunities, and possessions are entrusted gifts, not ultimate possessions.

Scripture calls believers to faithfulness rather than comparison. A steward is not judged by having the same resources as someone else, but by using what the Lord has given with obedience and love.

Christ is the Master who gives, calls, and returns. Stewardship is discipleship lived through ordinary responsibilities under His lordship.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people feel they have little to offer because they lack money, health, platform, or status. Stewardship reminds them that Christ can use what is entrusted to them, even when it seems small.

This doctrine also challenges waste and selfishness. What God gives is meant to be used for His glory, not consumed only for self.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask what God has entrusted to you right now. Offer your time, body, resources, story, gifts, and limitations to Christ, and use them faithfully by the Spirit’s strength.
